boundary.resolution: Sections 1 and 2 describe the two reading circuits, output control, local-memory input, and timing control. The opening figure separates their paths.

registers.resolution: Section 4 lists all 26 words, addresses, access rules, reset values, and decoded bit positions. Section 2.5 completes MMOD, AMOD, SLBG, and ALP operations. Unnamed retained bits are not must-zero bits.

datapath.resolution: Sections 2.1–2.5 specify geometry, interlace, two-byte local-memory words, packing, address equations and wrap, zero samples, composition order, RGB rounding and coefficient saturation, and separate alpha selection. Matching TS/C++ software is authoritative by explicit user decision; the deferred WebGPU discrepancy is recorded in pcrtc-webgpu-constant-blend.md.

visibility.resolution: Section 2.6 separates immediate programmed-word readback, the 22-word latch on VBlank entry before the system VBlank IRQ request, immediate beam restart on changed timing writes, and reset visibility. Separate writes can straddle the latch.

timing.resolution: Section 2.7 and the timing-register entries give the clock and timing equations, run conditions, reset landmarks, FIELD behavior, and changed-write restart hazard. The timeline is explicitly not to scale and is not a waveform.

interrupts.resolution: Sections 2.8 and 3.2 and the CSR/IMR entries cover HSINT/VSINT producers, the three retained event positions without normal producers, pending state, masks, acknowledgement, IRQ delivery, and the unmask race.

faults.resolution: Sections 2.10–2.11 establish ordinary CPU mapped-access widths, alignment, CPU modes, successive-word access, ignored high-word writes, synchronous exception causes, and the separate system bus fault latch. Pixel selectors and framebuffer wrap are deterministic, not format/address exceptions.

reset.resolution: Section 2.9 and CSR document action precedence, queued-input discard, accepted-work retirement, readback cancellation, partial-upload prefixes, reset versus flush scope, and the absence of local-memory clear/undo.

programming.resolution: Section 3 supplies ordered raw-word source/window and mask/acknowledge/unmask examples with explicit starting assumptions, derived values, latch visibility, output alpha, and the HSINT race. Hardware cautions are bounded by the sourced contracts.
